sections.markdown:
## C2 — Fog, hills, carbon monoxide, driving emergencies and confusables

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A75
Avoid driving in fog or a snowstorm unless absolutely necessary, and when visibility is limited, slow down enough to stop within the distance you can see. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A75
Use low beams in fog or heavy snow to cut the glare thrown back at you. [A75]
Why it matters: low beam is the right choice in fog because it reduces the glare reflected back at you.
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A75
If you cannot see, or tire from straining to see, pull fully off the road, leave the lights on, park and wait for better visibility. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F39 | anchor: A75
Narrow hilly or wooded roads hide blind pockets where another car may be only feet away before you see it, so use extra caution and tap the horn on dangerous curves. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F40 | anchor: A75
The law forbids coasting downhill with the transmission in neutral. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F41 | anchor: A75
Carbon monoxide poisoning is likelier in winter, when windows stay shut and engines are warmed up, and the fumes have no odor and can kill. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F42 | anchor: A75
Sudden weariness, yawning, dizziness and nausea signal carbon monoxide poisoning, and the only cure is plenty of fresh air. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F43 | anchor: A75
Prevent it by having the exhaust checked for leaks, not idling or driving with windows shut tight, and never warming up in a closed garage. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F44 | anchor: A75
In any emergency, think before you act, since instinct, like slamming the brakes in a skid, can be the wrong move. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F45 | anchor: A75
After a blowout, grip the wheel, steer straight, ease off the gas and do not brake until the car is under control; a thumping bulge can warn of one. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-F46 | anchor: A76
Under-inflation is one of the most common causes of blowouts, and a tire losing air fast pulls the car to one side. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F47 | anchor: A76
Losing a wheel gives the same warnings and needs the same response as a blowout: hold tight, steer straight, ease off the gas, no braking until slowed and in control. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F48 | anchor: A76
If steering fails, ease off the gas without braking or shifting, then brake very gently once the car has slowed. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F49 | anchor: A76
If the brake pedal sinks to the floor, pump it; a spongy, slowly sinking pedal is the usual early warning of brake failure. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F50 | anchor: A76
If pumping fails, apply the parking brake gently to avoid a skid, shift to a lower gear, or switch off the engine in gear, knowing power steering and brakes then stop assisting. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F51 | anchor: A76
If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, do not swerve back; stay on it, slow down, then ease gently back onto the pavement. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F52 | anchor: A76
If a car comes at you in your lane, pull right, slow down, sound the horn or flash lights at night, and never swerve into the left lane. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F53 | anchor: A76
If a passing car is stuck beside you, slow down when it can still get ahead, speed up when it must drop back, and move onto a good shoulder if a crash is nearly certain. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F54 | anchor: A77
A stalled manual car may be moved off tracks by running the starter in low or second gear, but an automatic has to be pushed. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F55 | anchor: A77
If a train is coming and the car will not move, leave it and walk beside the tracks toward the train so debris from the impact will not hit you. [A77]
Why it matters: walking toward the train sounds wrong, but the manual gives it as the way to stay clear of debris when the car is hit.
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F56 | anchor: A77
If your car lands in deep water and stays afloat, escape through a window right away, since opening a door lets water rush in. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F57 | anchor: A77
A sinking car usually goes down front first, leaving an air pocket in back; breathe there and escape through a window once it settles. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F58 | anchor: A77
For smoke from under the hood, pull off and turn off the ignition, and smother any fire with an extinguisher, dirt or sand, never water. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F59 | anchor: A77
In slow traffic, shifting to neutral and briefly racing the engine during stops helps prevent overheating; if steam appears, pull over, shut off the engine and do not open the radiator cap. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F60 | anchor: A77
If headlights fail, try the parking lights and turn signals; on a dark empty road, slow down on the pavement before moving onto the shoulder. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F61 | anchor: A77
If wipers fail in heavy rain or snow, or the hood flies up, slow down, look out the open side window, and get off the highway. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F62 | anchor: A77
A stuck accelerator may come free if you hook your toe under the pedal and lift; otherwise turn off the engine to slow down. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A71
Dim within 500 feet of oncoming traffic and within 200 feet behind a car, while headlights are required whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead. [A71]
Why it matters: group_hint headlight-distances; prereq_hint sec11-F03; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F05, sec11-F08.
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A76
A blowout, a lost wheel and a steering failure all call for easing off the gas instead of braking hard. [A76]
Why it matters: group_hint vehicle-failures; prereq_hint sec11-F44; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F47, sec11-F48.
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0076]
